contracts.ownership: run UUID plus dedicated exact label, strict full immutable ID parse. On collision, malformed identity, foreign label or daemon failure, cleanup fails visibly and never authorizes logs/removal. Verified IDs, rather than names, identify both cleanup commands.
contracts.uncertain_launch: launch_attempted is set before detached process call. Timeout still runs bounded ownership verification; recognized absence is distinct from daemon failure and retains the primary timeout.
contracts.failure_cleanup: log exit, log retention and interruption are captured without suppressing the following removal attempt. Removal errors remain failures even when conformance succeeded.
contracts.diagnostics: summary contains suite and cleanup errors. CLI rendering retains launch stderr, empty exception messages use type names, and combined failures preserve primary cause via exception chaining.
contracts.deadlines: readiness socket/TLS/inspection use remaining 30-second budget. Ownership/log/removal each have finite 30-second process timeouts; report copy also has 30 seconds. Adapter/build limits remain separate.
contracts.cancellation: KeyboardInterrupt during primary operation or log collection enters cleanup; successful cleanup reraises the original primary interruption, and a sole cleanup interruption retains identity. Multiple cleanup failures remain explicit.

rejected_hypotheses.hypothesis: A foreign container name may be force-removed after failed launch.
rejected_hypotheses.reason: Cleanup inspects the UUID label, validates full 64-character immutable ID, and stops before logs/rm on mismatch. Tests exercise collision and malformed output.

rejected_hypotheses.hypothesis: A log failure can hide removal failure or skip removal.
rejected_hypotheses.reason: Independent guarded steps collect both failures; JSON and CLI controls cover simultaneous suite/log/removal errors.

rejected_hypotheses.hypothesis: An uncertain launch is treated as no created resource.
rejected_hypotheses.reason: The attempt flag precedes docker run; cleanup still inspects ownership on subprocess timeout, with missing and daemon-failure branches distinguished.

limits: No Docker daemon, container, network socket, OpenSSL, Cargo or test execution was performed by this reviewer.
Mock subprocess tests establish command/error contracts; they do not prove live daemon cleanup or real signal delivery.
A daemon can complete creation after a timeout and an absent inspection. The run remains failed and retains UUID metadata for recovery; no proof of remote cancellation is claimed.
Unrecognized absence wording conservatively fails instead of guessing ownership.
If diagnostic filesystem writes fail, bytes cannot be retained; errors remain in exception/CLI output.
